schema_description: Living Hearing Profile — sovereign, user-owned, versioned hearing data. Extends openhear-audiogram-v1 with preference, context, haptic and history layers.
subject: Lewis Burgess

clinical_core.comment: Immutable clinical measurements. Append only via history layer; never mutate in place.
clinical_core.source: Dorothy Thomson Hearing Services, 12 Southend Ave, Darlington, DL3 7HL
clinical_core.notes: Most recent verified clinical audiogram. ISQ (no significant change) from prior tests dating back to 2017-01-19. High-frequency sloping sensorineural loss — the public reference profile for OpenHear.

preference_layer.comment: User-defined loudness and comfort preferences. Evolves over time as the user fine-tunes their experience. Refined 2026-08-12 and further strengthened 2026-08-16 after additional lived-experience feedback on listening effort and familiar vs unfamiliar talkers.

loudness_growth.comment: Per-frequency gain offset applied on top of clinical prescription. Positive = louder, negative = quieter. Mid-frequency lift prioritised for speech intelligibility under high-frequency sloping loss.

preference_layer.notes: Stronger mid-band lift (1–2 kHz) after real-world confirmation that speech clarity in this region reduces listening fatigue for sloping losses. Additional 2026-08-16 signal: sustained listening effort frequently leads to ‘switching off’ — preference layer and haptic support should aim to lower cognitive load, not only raise audibility. When an Auracast clean feed is active, preference offsets still apply; aggressive room-noise strategies should step down.

context_map.comment: Situational listening presets. Expanded 2026-08-12 and 2026-08-16 with lived-experience signals; 2026-08-19 added auracast_venue for Bluetooth LE Audio broadcast clean feeds in public spaces (see docs/AURACAST.md).

contexts.name: familiar_speaker
contexts.label: Known / familiar talker (e.g. partner or regular voice)
contexts.notes: Lived-experience signal (2026-08-16): familiar voices (especially a long-term partner) remain markedly easier to understand than novel accents or unexpected conversational shifts. Supports lower processing aggression and reduced haptic load when the talker is known.

contexts.name: noisy_environment
contexts.label: Pub, restaurant, crowded social space
contexts.notes: Persistent failure mode even with modern aids on loud settings. Residual environmental awareness (traffic, birds, doorbell) can remain while speech intelligibility collapses. Primary target for haptic speech-support and effort reduction.

contexts.name: clinical_environment
contexts.label: Hospital ward / ICU — alarms + concurrent speech
contexts.notes: Direct insight from paediatric/neonatal clinician participant: amplified alarms frequently mask concurrent speech. Prefer selective haptic routing for alarms while preserving speech band.

contexts.name: phone_call
contexts.label: Telephone / video call
contexts.notes: Streaming to aids can work for expected conversational strands; performance drops when the topic shifts or the speaker is unfamiliar. Context-switch difficulty is cognitive as well as acoustic.

contexts.name: transport
contexts.label: Public transport — announcements and carriage noise

contexts.name: auracast_venue
contexts.label: Auracast / LE Audio broadcast — clean feed in a public space
contexts.notes: Bluetooth LE Audio Auracast delivers the original clean source (announcement, stage mic, TV channel, language track) rather than room acoustics. Prefer preference-layer shaping over aggressive room-noise strategies. Continuous stream speech should not drive continuous haptic voice pulses; haptic remains for discrete environmental events the broadcast does not cover, plus short join/leave cues. See docs/AURACAST.md.

haptic_layer.comment: Haptic substitution weights. Higher weight = stronger haptic signal for that sound category. Severity-weighted from the audiogram and further refined with real-world priorities (alarms, infant cry, speech). 2026-08-16: reinforced role of haptics as a non-surgical bridge for people who remain above cochlear-implant speech-recognition thresholds yet still cannot follow conversation in noise. 2026-08-19: when an Auracast clean feed is active, continuous stream speech should not generate continuous voice haptics; reserve haptic for discrete safety/environmental events and short broadcast join/leave cues.

sound_classes.name: voice
sound_classes.note: Speech — highest priority in acoustic scenes. When an Auracast clean feed is carrying continuous speech, do not drive continuous haptic voice pulses; keep haptic for discrete events the broadcast does not replace.

sound_classes.name: alarm
sound_classes.note: Safety critical. Maximum haptic at the high-frequency band where this profile has the greatest loss. Route preferentially to haptic in clinical_environment context. Remains active even when an Auracast stream is joined.

sound_classes.name: infant_cry
sound_classes.note: Added 2026-08-12 from clinician participant insight (neonatal/paediatric). High urgency for future parent scenarios and clinical environments.

sound_classes.name: doorbell
sound_classes.note: High loss at 2 kHz drives strong substitution

sound_classes.name: traffic
sound_classes.note: Low-frequency traffic noise — kept lower priority than speech and safety sounds

sound_classes.name: media
sound_classes.note: General media — user can raise if desired

history.comment: Append-only change log with SHA-256 content commitments (Burgess Principle compatible). Each entry records what changed and a hash of the profile state at that point.

entries.author: Lewis Burgess
entries.description: Added loudness-growth offsets based on six months of real-world listening experience. Slight mid-frequency boost preferred in conversation.

entries.author: Lewis Burgess
entries.description: Added five contextual listening presets. Active context set to quiet_conversation.

entries.author: Lewis Burgess
entries.description: Added severity-weighted haptic substitution map for wristband.

entries.author: Lewis Burgess
entries.description: First authentic non-placeholder commitment. Profile advanced from static 2021 clinical snapshot to a true Living Hearing Profile. Expanded context map with clinical/ICU and social-noise environments drawn from RNID Research Panel participant insights (12 Aug 2026). Strengthened mid-frequency preference offsets for speech under high-frequency sloping loss. Added infant_cry haptic class and raised priority of alarms and speech.

entries.author: Lewis Burgess
entries.description: Incorporated further RNID-panel lived-experience signals: (1) familiar voices remain markedly easier than novel accents or unexpected conversational shifts — added familiar_speaker context; (2) people can retain environmental awareness with aids while speech-in-noise and group conversation still fail — reinforced noisy_environment and phone_call notes; (3) the ‘cusp of implant’ functional gap (above speech-recognition threshold for CI yet still unable to follow conversation in noise) is a primary use-case for non-surgical haptic substitution; (4) sustained listening effort leading to switching-off is now explicit in preference notes. Profile continues to evolve from real user reports rather than laboratory assumptions.

entries.author: Lewis Burgess
entries.description: Recorded complementary relationship with Bluetooth LE Audio Auracast. Added auracast_venue context for clean broadcast feeds in public spaces. Preference and haptic notes updated so continuous stream speech does not drive continuous voice haptics; discrete join/leave cues and residual environmental/safety events remain. See docs/AURACAST.md. Auracast delivers the clean source; OpenHear delivers personal, sovereign, context-aware shaping and haptic substitution on top of whatever the person can hear — including a clean feed when one is available.
